chunks: Yunus narrated from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who struck a man unjustly, so the man repulsed him from himself, so he was hit by something. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him'.

key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is nothing upon him (no liability)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on self-defense when repelling an unjust attacker?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in cases of unjust aggression, the victim's right to self-defense is absolute, meaning any injury inflicted upon the aggressor while repelling the attack incurs no financial liability (diyah). This ruling underscores the principle of 'no harm' (la darar) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing self-defense from retaliation where proportional compensation might otherwise be required. It highlights the legal protection of the individual's honor and body against arbitrary aggression.
